summary: trip ships through a two-step Release workflow. Someone starts the workflow by hand and picks which part of the version to raise. The workflow then opens a release pull request, like this one, that changes only the version. Merging that pull request is the decision to ship.
This pull request raises trip's version from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2. It changes one line in Cargo.toml and the matching line in Cargo.lock, and nothing else.
When it merges, the workflow's publish job runs .github/scripts/release.py tag on the merge commit. That command does three things in order:

1. Tags the release. It pushes the v0.2.2 tag, which never moves once pushed.
  2. Publishes the GitHub release. It creates the release for v0.2.2 with notes generated from the merged pull requests.
  3. Moves the major tag. It moves v0 to the new release last. The installer follows v0, and trip upgrade reads the newest GitHub release.

cards.title: What the review checked
cards.html:
• 0.2.2 is above every vX.Y.Z tag on the repository. The tags are v0.2.0 and v0.2.1.
  • The trip entry in Cargo.lock names the same version as Cargo.toml.
  • The commit sits directly on the current head of main and changes only the two version files.
  • The Check workflow passed on this exact head, in the run the Release workflow dispatched.

cards.title: Why the checks list looks short
cards.html: The pull request's checks list shows only the Vercel checks. GitHub doesn't attach a run started with workflow_dispatch to a pull request's checks, so the dispatched Check run's check and msrv jobs appear only on the commit. Both passed. A second Check run, started by the pull_request event, is waiting for approval and hasn't run.

groups.title: The version bump
groups.kicker: The two files that carry trip's version
intro: The release script treats Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock as trip's two version files. It refuses a release commit that changes any other file, or that changes either file beyond its version line.
Cargo.toml declares the version. Cargo.lock records the same version in its entry for the trip package, and cargo build --locked fails when the two disagree.

checks.text: The diff from main changes exactly these two files, one line each, and each changed line is the version. I read both files at the head and compared them with the base.

files.note: The package version moves from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2.

checks.text: 0.2.2 is above the newest release tag, v0.2.1, so the publish job's version check accepts it. I listed the repository's tags with git ls-remote --tags.

files.note: The lockfile's entry for the trip package follows the new version.

checks.text: This is the lockfile's only trip entry, and its version matches Cargo.toml.
